metadata.title: 1970 Case 42
metadata.original_presentation: A 56-year-old woman was admitted to the hospital because of weakness of the shoulders, arms and neck.

required.content: What is the patient's history of presenting illness?
required.response: The patient had been well until three years previously, when she began to experience difficulty in swallowing solids. Over the next two years, the dysphagia progressed, and she lost 18 kg in weight. One year before entry, she was admitted to another hospital, where a stricture was found in the lower portion of the esophagus; a thoracotomy was performed, with repair of the stricture and symptomatic improvement. Eight months before admission, she experienced loss of hearing in the left ear, accompanied by mild dizziness. Six months before entry, mild dysphagia recurred, with soreness in the left side of the neck and throat. Two months before admission, she began to have progressive weakness and mild soreness of both arms and shoulders. Three weeks before entry, the neck muscles became weak, and the voice faint. During the week before admission, dyspnea developed.

teaching_points.content: Progressive dysphagia and weight loss can indicate esophageal or neurological disorders.
Hearing loss and dizziness may suggest cranial nerve involvement.
Progressive muscle weakness and dyspnea can be signs of neuromuscular disorders.

current_ideal_differential_diagnosis.name: Myasthenia Gravis
supporting_evidence: progressive weakness of shoulders, arms, and neck
refuting_evidence: hearing loss and dizziness are not typical features
additional_information_needed: CT scan of the chest to check for thymoma

current_ideal_differential_diagnosis.name: Polymyositis
supporting_evidence: progressive weakness of shoulders and arms
mild soreness of arms and shoulders
refuting_evidence: hearing loss and dizziness are not typical features

current_ideal_differential_diagnosis.name: Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis (ALS)
supporting_evidence: progressive weakness of shoulders, arms, and neck
refuting_evidence: hearing loss and dizziness are not typical features

current_ideal_differential_diagnosis.name: Multiple Sclerosis
refuting_evidence: hearing loss and dizziness are not classic features
additional_information_needed: MRI of the brain and spinal cord
lumbar puncture for cerebrospinal fluid analysis

current_ideal_differential_diagnosis.name: Paraneoplastic Syndrome
refuting_evidence: hearing loss and dizziness are not typical features

required.content: What were the findings on physical examination?
required.response: The patient was severely dehydrated and cachectic, with a whispering voice and a weak cough. Neurologic examination showed moderate loss of recent memory, mild left facial paresis, absent hearing in the left ear, marked atrophy of several muscles, fasciculations, and marked weakness of proximal muscles of the shoulder girdle. Sensory examination revealed diminished pain and temperature sensations in certain cervical segments. Reflexes were diminished or absent in the arms, and the plantar responses were flexor.

teaching_points.content: Muscle atrophy and fasciculations are indicative of lower motor neuron lesions.
Diminished reflexes and sensory loss can help localize neurological lesions.

current_ideal_differential_diagnosis.name: Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis (ALS)
supporting_evidence: progressive weakness of shoulders, arms, and neck
refuting_evidence: sensory deficits are not typical in ALS
additional_information_needed: MRI of the brain and spinal cord
genetic testing if familial ALS is suspected

current_ideal_differential_diagnosis.name: Myasthenia Gravis
key_features: muscle weakness that worsens with activity
supporting_evidence: progressive weakness of shoulders, arms, and neck
additional_information_needed: CT scan of the chest to check for thymoma

current_ideal_differential_diagnosis.name: Multiple Sclerosis
key_features: neurological deficits that vary over time
refuting_evidence: progressive nature without remissions is atypical
additional_information_needed: MRI of the brain and spinal cord

current_ideal_differential_diagnosis.name: Bulbar Palsy
additional_information_needed: neurological examination focusing on cranial nerves

current_ideal_differential_diagnosis.name: Cervical Spondylotic Myelopathy
refuting_evidence: progressive nature without remissions is atypical
additional_information_needed: neurological examination focusing on gait and coordination

required.content: What were the results of the diagnostic tests performed?
required.response: X-ray films of the skull and mastoid views disclosed no abnormality. A contrast study of the left posterior fossa was negative. Chest X-ray revealed minimal left ventricular prominence and clear lungs. Cerebrospinal fluid analysis showed clear fluid with 2 lymphocytes per cubic millimeter and protein of 21 mg per 100 ml. Blood tests showed a white-cell count of 13,000 with 81% neutrophils, and other values were within normal limits. Cervical spine films showed degenerative changes and osteophytic spurs. A cervical myelographic study showed a normal-sized spinal cord with no evidence of syrinx or Arnold-Chiari malformation.

teaching_points.content: Normal imaging of the brain and skull can help rule out central causes of neurological symptoms.
Cervical spine changes can contribute to neurological symptoms through nerve compression.

current_ideal_differential_diagnosis.name: Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis (ALS)
supporting_evidence: progressive weakness of shoulders, arms, and neck
marked weakness of proximal muscles of the shoulder girdle
refuting_evidence: mild left facial paresis and absent hearing in the left ear are atypical for ALS
additional_information_needed: Electromyography (EMG) to assess for denervation and reinnervation patterns typical of ALS

current_ideal_differential_diagnosis.name: Myasthenia Gravis
key_features: muscle weakness that worsens with activity
supporting_evidence: progressive weakness of shoulders, arms, and neck
refuting_evidence: absence of ptosis or ocular involvement

current_ideal_differential_diagnosis.name: Cervical Spondylotic Myelopathy
supporting_evidence: soreness in the left side of the neck
diminished pain and temperature sensations in certain cervical segments
degenerative changes and osteophytic spurs on cervical spine films
refuting_evidence: normal-sized spinal cord with no evidence of syrinx or Arnold-Chiari malformation
additional_information_needed: MRI of the cervical spine to assess for spinal cord compression

current_ideal_differential_diagnosis.name: Multiple Sclerosis
key_features: neurological deficits separated in time and space
supporting_evidence: diminished pain and temperature sensations in certain cervical segments
additional_information_needed: MRI of the brain and spinal cord to look for demyelinating lesions

required.content: What management decisions and treatments were made during the hospital stay?
required.response: Fluids were given intravenously. Prednisone was started at 60 mg daily and later reduced to 40 mg daily. Chlorpromazine was begun. A nasogastric tube was passed for feeding. Oxygen was administered via a nasal catheter.

teaching_points.content: Corticosteroids like prednisone are used to reduce inflammation and immune response.
Supportive care, including nutritional support and oxygen therapy, is crucial in managing severe cases.
